🧠 Crypto News Brief: Washington's agencies are moving fast to fill the vacuum left by the failed CLARITY Act, while state-linked hacking and sanctions dominate the security beat. Bitcoin drifted back toward $80,000 after Friday's rebound. 🏛️ Regulators race to replace the failed CLARITY Act With the market-structure bill dead in the Senate for now, the SEC and CFTC are substituting their own rulemaking for legislation. The CFTC has already sent a crypto market proposal to the White House for review, and the SEC has opened a conditional five-year path for tokenized stock venues. Analysts warn that agency rules are far easier to unwind than a statute would have been. Read full story 🕵️ FBI and Japan name North Korean crew behind a $10.7M wallet raid Seven agencies from four countries published a joint advisory on the group tracked as WaterPlum, which posed as AI, crypto and NFT recruiters to plant malware during fake coding tests. At least 30,000 devices in over 100 countries were infected between December 2025 and July 2026, with funds or credentials pulled from more than 7,000 wallets. More details 🇪🇺 Lagarde personally intervened to block Binance's EU licence The Wall Street Journal reports that the ECB president asked Greek officials not to approve Binance's MiCA application, even though the central bank has no formal licensing role. Athens had already signalled to ESMA that it intended to approve; Binance withdrew in June and remains locked out of a passport covering the whole bloc. Read more 🔓 Haruko breach exposes trading data of 15 institutional clients Attackers pulled an access token out of one of the London firm's internal processes and reached read-only exchange API credentials and trading records belonging to 15 customers. Smaller hedge funds without IP whitelisting may have lost a modest amount of assets. Haruko says the hole is patched and a technical post-mortem is coming. See details ⚓ US sanctions the exchange behind Iran's bitcoin toll booth Treasury designated Tehran-based BitBank, alleging it moved hundreds of millions of dollars in bitcoin to the Revolutionary Guards and processed passage fees collected from tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz. The dubious evidence for sunshine supplements

Senior science writer



 Most doctors are dubious about the merits of supplements, pointing out that many of them have no evidence to suggest that they are safe, or that they work as advertised.
